issues.body: `_live_nodes` prunes literal-dead branches and deferred scopes, but otherwise enumerates children without statement-order control flow. Consequently a candidate such as `targets = starvation_park_targets(...); return; for target in targets: park_starved_partition_holder(...)` is certified as `tick`, even though no invocation can reach the loop. The same problem occurs when the park call follows an unconditional `return`, `raise`, `break`, or `continue` in its enclosing block. The added comment explicitly says earlier `return`/`raise` is not seen but then claims that direction REFUSES; the implementation actually accepts when the binding, loop, and call remain syntactically present. None of the 17 table rows exercises this case, so the new tests do not catch it.
issues.fix_hint: Make the accepting traversal conservatively account for sequential terminators (including terminators inside the relevant enclosing block/control-flow shape), or explicitly narrow the claimed guarantee and ensure the seam fails closed for unsupported control-flow shapes. Add red-on-regression rows with the loop after `return`/`raise` and the call after `break`/`continue`, plus live control cases so an unconditional refusal cannot satisfy the suite.
issues.title: The reachability seam accepts code after an unconditional return or raise

verdict.summary: The new traversal rejects the two added syntactic cases, but it is not a sound reachability check: it still certifies calls that are unconditionally unreachable after an earlier control-flow terminator. This directly contradicts the new documentation's claim that the earlier-return/raise direction refuses and leaves the marquee structural proof vulnerable. Round 1, so progress is null.
